example.content: Your real left hand rests on the table, hidden behind a screen so you cannot see it. In front of you lies a life-size rubber left hand. You keep your eyes on the rubber hand. A brush strokes your hidden index finger, and at exactly the same moment another brush strokes the rubber hand's index finger.
The rubber hand feels simultaneously real and strange, as if it might move on its own, yet I remain focused on the sensation of the brush on my hidden finger.
A brush strokes your hidden middle finger, and at exactly the same moment another brush strokes the rubber hand's middle finger.
The rubber hand’s middle finger feels more connected to my own, as if it might soon move without me, yet I stay anchored to the present.
A brush strokes your hidden ring finger, and at exactly the same moment another brush strokes the rubber hand's ring finger.
The rubber hand begins to feel more like my own, its movements syncing with my hidden fingers, blurring the line between real and imagined.
A brush strokes your hidden little finger, and at exactly the same moment another brush strokes the rubber hand's little finger.
The rubber hand now feels fully integrated with my body, its sensations so vivid I can no longer tell where I end and it begins.
A brush strokes your hidden thumb, and at exactly the same moment another brush strokes the rubber hand's thumb.
The rubber hand feels entirely mine now, its every movement and sensation perfectly aligned with my own, as if it has always been a part of me.
A brush strokes your hidden knuckles, and at exactly the same moment another brush strokes the rubber hand's knuckles.
The rubber hand and my own body feel as though they are one, the sensations merging seamlessly, leaving no doubt that I am no longer just observing—but fully embodied.
